# New renderings — iliad-109 (17.106–197)

Rows in the format of the conventions table. Wording reused from the Odyssey is marked as such; none departs from a shipped Odyssey or Iliad rendering of the same Greek.

| Greek | `l` | `i` | avoided on purpose |
|---|---|---|---|
| θεσπέσιον … φόβον ἔμβαλε (17.118) | "wondrous flight … cast" | "had cast wondrous flight among them" | "terror" (the departure at 11.402 is for a verb of seizing and, as the table says at 15.522, is not repeated), "fear", "panic" (reserved for φύζα); φόβος in battle is "flight" (5.252, 12.432), as in ἐν φόβον ὄρσῃ "rouses flight among them"; ἐμβάλλω "throw in"; θεσπέσιος keeps "wondrous" |
| ἐπακτῆρες (ἄνδρες ἐπακτῆρες, 17.135) | "men, hunters" | "hunters" | "huntsmen", "beaters", "dog-handlers"; reused from odyssey-096 (19.435, "the hunters"); ἐπακτήρ is from ἐπάγω "bring on" |
| ἐπισκύνιον (17.136) | "the brow" | "its whole brow" | "forehead", "eyebrows", "frown"; the skin above the eyes |
| παχνοῦται (ἦτορ, 17.112) | "is chilled" | "is chilled" | "freezes", "stiffens with fear", "grows cold with fear" (each adds a cause the Greek does not state); from πάχνη "hoarfrost" |
| ἠΰτε πύργον (17.128) | published (iliad-043, 7.219) | published | none; the line is unchanged except that this unit ends at the semicolon |
| φύξηλις (17.143) | "a runaway" | "runaway" (+ note: rare word, from φεύγω "flee"; exact shade not known) | "coward" (reserved for κακός in the sense the note gives), "skulker", "fugitive"; the note says the word is rare and not certain |
| κλέος ἐσθλόν (αὔτως κλέος ἐσθλὸν ἔχει, 17.143) | "good glory" | "good glory" | "noble fame", "fair repute", "a name"; follows the table’s κλέος ἐσθλόν "good glory" (5.273) |
| λαοῖς (σὺν λαοῖς τοὶ Ἰλίῳ ἐγγεγάασιν, 17.145) | "the people" | "the people" | "troops" (the table’s `i` for λαοί of an army, 2.577–580, but these are the townspeople born in Ilium, set against the allies; the exception of 2.664 "people" is followed), "peoples", "men" |
| πεφήσεται (Τροίῃ δὲ πεφήσεται αἰπὺς ὄλεθρος, 17.155) | "will be shown" | "will show itself" (+ note: taken as a reduplicated future passive of φαίνω; the derivation is not certain) | "will be slain", "will be brought to Troy" (each decides a disputed derivation); αἰπὺς ὄλεθρος keeps "steep destruction" (6.327) |
| δῆρις (πόνον καὶ δῆριν, 17.158) | "contest" | "contest" | "strife", "battle" (reserved for μάχη), "struggle"; keeps δῆρις "contest" (ἀδήριτος "undecided", 17.42) |
| ἐρυσαίμεθα χάρμης (17.161) | "drag him out of the joy of battle" | "drag him out of the joy of battle" | "out of the fight", "from the battle" (loses χάρμη); the table’s χάρμη "the joy of battle" (4.222, 4.509) kept with the genitive of separation |
| λύσειαν (ἔντεα καλὰ λύσειαν, 17.163) | "would release" | "would give up" (+ note: λύω "loose, release", as in a ransom) | "would strip" (the Argives are the ones giving the gear up, not taking it), "would surrender", "would ransom"; λύω keeps "release" (1.401) in `l` |
| ἀγχέμαχοι θεράποντες (17.165, with the verb left out) | "close-fighting attendants" | "and who has close-fighting attendants" | "and we, close-fighting attendants" (the published 16.272 reads the nominative as "we"; here there is no "we" to read it with, so the verb is supplied as "has"); the table’s ἀγχέμαχοι θεράποντες "close-fighting attendants" otherwise unchanged |
| ἐτάλασσας (οὐκ ἐτάλασσας στήμεναι, 17.166) | "did not dare" | "did not dare" | "did not bring yourself" (kept for ἔτλης, 17.153), "endured", "had the heart"; ἐτάλασσα is a rare aorist from the root of τλάω |
| ἄντα κατ’ ὄσσε ἰδών (17.167) | "to stand against him, looking him in the eyes" | "to stand against … looking him in the eyes" | "face to face", "eye to eye", "looking him in the face"; the Greek says "eyes" |
| δηΐων ἐν ἀϋτῇ (17.167) | "in the battle-cry of enemies" | "in the battle-cry of enemies" | "in the battle", "in the din of foes"; the table’s ἀϋτή "battle-cry" and δήϊοι "enemies’" (2.544) |
| ὑπέροπλον ἔειπες (17.170) | "arrogantly have you spoken" | "spoken so arrogantly" | "presumptuously"; the table’s ὑπέροπλον "arrogantly" (15.185) |
| ὠνοσάμην πάγχυ φρένας (17.173) | published (iliad-086, 14.95) | published | none |
| πελώριον (Αἴαντα πελώριον, 17.174) | "huge" | "huge" | "monstrous" (the Odyssey’s l), "gigantic"; follows the table’s πελώριος "huge" (3.166, 5.594) |
| ἔρριγα (οὔ τοι ἐγὼν ἔρριγα μάχην, 17.175) | "shudder at" | "shudder at" | "shrink from", "fear" (reserved for δείδω); follows the table’s ἔρριγ’ ἀντιβολῆσαι "shudders to meet" (7.114) |
| κτύπον ἵππων (17.175) | "the din of horses" | "the din of horses" | "the thunder of hooves", "the clatter of chariots"; κτύπος "din" |
| ὁτὲ δ’ αὐτὸς ἐποτρύνει μαχέσασθαι (17.178) | "and at another time himself urges him on to fight" | "and at another time himself urges a man on to fight" | the published "when he himself urges him on to fight" (16.690) — there ὅτε is the conjunction; here ὁτὲ is printed with the accent of "at another time", so the English is not the published one |
| κακός ἔσσομαι (17.180) | "base I shall be" | "a coward" | "bad", "poor"; κακός "base" (the table’s κάκ’ ἐλέγχεα "base disgraces", 2.235); the coward sense is carried in `i` and the note |
| πανημέριος (17.180) | "all day long" | "all day long" | "for the whole day", "all through the day", "the livelong day" |
| ἀλκῆς μάλα περ μεμαῶτα (17.181) | "though greatly eager for might" | "however eager for might" | "for valour", "for battle" (valour is kept for ἀλκή only where the table says); ἀλκή "might" (4.234, 5.299) |
| ἀγχιμαχηταί (Τρῶες καὶ Λύκιοι καὶ Δάρδανοι ἀγχιμαχηταί, 17.184) | "close-fighters" | "you fighters at close quarters" | "close-fighting" as an adjective (the table’s ἀγχέμαχος is the adjective); follows the table’s ἀγχιμαχητής (2.604); Δάρδανοι "Dardanians" (7.348) |
| ὄφρ’ ἂν … δύω (17.186) | "until I … put on" | "until I have put on" | "while I put on" (the aorist subjunctive with ἄν is "until"; the table’s ὄφρ’ ἂν "until", 1.509), "so that I may put on" (purpose); δύω "put on" (the table’s δύσετο τεύχεα καλά, 13.241) |
| ἐνάριξα … κατακτάς (17.187) | "I despoiled … having killed" | "I stripped off … when I killed" | "I slew" (kept for ἐναίρω), "despoiled" in `i`; ἐναρίζω "strip a slain man" (5.155) |
| Πατρόκλοιο βίην (17.187) | "the might of Patroclus" | "the might of Patroclus" | "mighty Patroclus", "Patroclus himself" (each erases the periphrasis); follows Πριάμοιο βίην (3.105) and βίη Ἡρακληείη (2.658) |
| δηΐου ἐκ πολέμοιο (17.189) | "out of the hostile war" | "out of the hostile war" | "from the enemy’s war", "from the fighting"; δήϊος "hostile" (2.415) and πόλεμος "war" |
| ποσὶ κραιπνοῖσι μετασπών (17.190) | "with rushing feet following after" | "following after them on rushing feet" | "swift feet" (kept for ταχέες πόδες), "in pursuit"; follows the table’s κραιπνοῖσι ποσί "rushing feet" (6.505) and μετασπόμενος "following after" (13.567) |
| πολυδάκρυος (μάχης πολυδακρύου, 17.192) | "of many tears" | "of many tears" | "tearful" (kept for δακρυόεις, 13.765), "full of weeping", "much-weeping" (active, wrong); πολυ- "many" + δάκρυ "tear" |
| ἔντε’ ἄμειβεν (17.192) | "his gear he was exchanging" | "exchanged his gear" | "changed his armour" (armour is reserved for τεύχεα); follows ἀρήϊα τεύχεα ἄμειβον "exchanged" (the table) and ἔντεα "gear" |
| ὃ μὲν τὰ ἃ δῶκε … ὃ δ’ … δῦνε (17.193–194) | "Indeed he, on the one hand, his own gear gave … and he on the other hand … was putting on" | "Hector, on the one hand, gave his own gear … and he, on the other hand, put on" | "one of them … the other" (both are Hector); ἅ possessive "his own", kept apart from the relative ἅ of 195 |
| Οὐρανίωνες (17.195) | "the Uranians" | "the gods of heaven" | follows the table (5.373), unchanged |
| ὄπασσε (ᾧ παιδὶ ὄπασσε γηράς, 17.196–197) | "bestowed" | "passed them on" | "gave" (kept for ἔπορον, ἔδωκε), "left"; ὀπάζω "bestow, make follow" |
